notes: NOT CITED / UNVERIFIED Siemens Energy Charlotte: the Charlotte city news page and the Mecklenburg County news page were opened and contain no Siemens transformer announcement. Siemens is also said to have described more than 80% of U.S. large power transformers as imported (search summary only).

Hitachi Energy South Boston: the 2025 WDBJ7 article quotes completion 'by 2028'; the June 2026 WDBJ7 article quotes completion 'sometime in 2029'. Dates conflict; the 2026 article is the newer one. Acreage and square footage are absent from both pages. The 10 acres Halifax County donated are for workforce housing, not the plant. Campus employs 850 today per the 2026 article. A separate roughly $25M, roughly 100-job large distribution transformer expansion at South Boston appears in a Supply Chain 247 search snippet, not opened, and is unverified.

Prolec GE Goldsboro: WRAL (search snippet, not opened) reports about 375 current employees. Company release says the expansion will double Goldsboro manufacturing capacity by 2030 and add 200 units per year. A trade report (not opened) gives medium-transformer output rising from 220 to 420 units per year. Groundbreaking March 17, 2026 and a state JDIG grant of about $4.7M appear only in search snippets and are unverified. Goldsboro beat sites in Wisconsin, Louisiana, Mexico and Brazil (snippet). No prior use of the site stated.

HD Hyundai Electric Montgomery: the T&D World article gives about 312,000 sq ft for the new facility, and the company's Montgomery campus is described as the largest U.S. power transformer production site. Jobs (about 200) and a $150M revenue figure appear only in search summaries, not quoted, so jobs is set to null. Completion is quoted as 'April next year' from a March 2026 article, giving April 2027. Ulsan, Korea expansion is linked (summary, unverified).

Eaton Jonesville: the Business Wire release returned HTTP 403, so facts come from the Area Development page, which quotes the 2025-02-15 announcement. The 861,000 sq ft building is an existing facility being retrofitted, but the page gives no prior use, so brownfield and former_use are null. A separate Henrico County, Virginia campus is mentioned in the Business Wire headline and is not part of this row. Production scheduled to begin in 2027.

Hyosung HICO Memphis: a May 2025 $51M expansion adding 123 jobs (360,000 sq ft facility on a 200-acre plot in South Memphis) appears in search results only and is unverified. Governor's office cites $157M while Governor Lee cites $150M for the 765-kV plant. The Memphis plant was purchased in 2019 from Mitsubishi Electric (summary). Target of being the number one U.S. large power transformer supplier by 2027 is in a summary.

Cleveland-Cliffs Butler Works: the WPXI article's '$170 million investment' refers to an earlier investment that helped save Butler Works, not the GOES expansion cost, so investment_usd is null. A $200M GOES expansion figure appears in a Webull summary (not opened) and is unresolved. The DOE $75M grant is verified from WPXI (dated 2026-04-22), but the program name is not on the fetched page and needs checking against energy.gov. Replacing gas-fired slab reheat furnaces with induction furnaces at Butler is reported in a 2025 source (not opened). Claim that Butler is the sole U.S. GOES producer is a search summary and needs checking. Weirton, WV transformer plant: 2024 annual report (snippet) cites a $50M WVEDA co-investment; a later report says Cliffs halted capital toward it. Status unresolved. Not written as a facility row.

Virginia Transformer Rincon: the fetched company page gives 400 jobs, 50% capacity increase and March 2027 completion, but no dollar figure. The $40M investment comes from a search headline (plantservices) and a Governor's office description, not opened, so investment_usd is null. A separate '70% productivity' claim exists in a snippet and measures a different thing. A new greenfield plant at Shoals Research Airpark, Colbert County, Alabama, is announced May 2026: 600,000 sq ft, 1,100 jobs (search summary, not opened). Candidate for a future row, unverified.

WEG Washington MO: fetched DED release gives $77M and 50 jobs but no completion year. The 2028 completion, 560 workforce across three Washington plants, Chapter 100 bonds, and the 50% capacity increase are from search summaries (Missourian and other sources), not opened. Missourian describes the work as renovation and expansion of the oldest of WEG's three Washington plants, which is not a statement that the site was previously industrial, so brownfield is null. An earlier $10M, 40-50 job expansion is also mentioned (undated).

Pennsylvania Transformer Technology: the fetched state release gives $102.5M, 217 jobs, 300,000 sq ft across two new facilities in Raeford (headline says 200 jobs; body says 217), and an $800,000 One North Carolina Fund grant. Groundbreaking December 10, 2025, a $400,000 NCRR grant, and the Canonsburg plant (1.1M sq ft building, about 700,000 sq ft used for transformer and voltage regulator manufacturing, local report) are from unopened sources. Canonsburg itself has no separate expansion figures found.

DOE awards: the only DOE award verified in this pass is the $75M grant to Cleveland-Cliffs (see above). No 2025 DOE award to a distribution transformer manufacturer was found. Search results show an $18M DOE Flexible Innovative Transformer Technologies (FITT) funding opportunity (funding opportunity only, no award confirmed), and a congressional request for $600M for domestic transformer manufacturing that is not confirmed as enacted. The grid-equipment DOE award search did not reach energy.gov selection announcements; GRIP is the next place to check.
